title: Folding a Paper: A Small Synthetic Study

sections.title: Abstract
sections.takeaway: Folded reading lets readers move between a paper's words and its summaries

sentences: We study how readers move between a paper's own words and short summaries of it.
Readers who could fold the text found the main claims faster than readers of the plain text.
We describe the reader and its limits.
units.key: Readers who fold the text find the main claims faster. They moved between a paper's words and its summaries.
units.takeaway: Readers who fold the text find the main claims faster

sections.title: Introduction
sections.takeaway: Readers skim papers, and summaries lose the author's exact words

sentences: Researchers read many papers each week [1, 2].
Most of that reading is skimming for the main claim (Lee et al., 2021).
Skimming saves time but misses how a claim is argued.
units.key: Most reading is skimming for the main claim. Skimming misses how a claim is argued.
units.takeaway: Most reading is skimming for the main claim

sentences: Summaries written by language models are short.
They do not show which of the author's sentences they rest on.
No reader we know links each summary line back to the text.
units.key: Model summaries do not show the sentences they rest on. No reader links each summary line back to the text.
units.takeaway: Model summaries do not show the sentences they rest on

sections.title: Method
sections.takeaway: The reader folds each paragraph into five levels and links them to the PDF

sentences: Each paragraph is folded into five levels, from a topic to the full text.
A word keeps its place across levels when it appears in both, scored by $s = n / N$.
The PDF beside the text is matched by runs of three words.
units.key: Each paragraph folds into five levels. The PDF beside the text is matched by runs of three words.
units.takeaway: Each paragraph folds into five levels

sections.title: Results
sections.takeaway: Readers found claims faster with folds

sentences: Twelve readers found the main claim in 41 seconds with folds and 68 seconds without.
The gap held for long papers (Figure 1).
units.key: Readers found the main claim faster with folds. They took 41 seconds instead of 68.
units.takeaway: Readers found the main claim faster with folds
